record.population: 31 relevant reports of mercury poisoning from lightening cosmetics (to March 2011)
record.design: Toxicology review of case reports and product analyses
record.finding: Mercury and its salts are prohibited as skin-lightening agents because of high toxicity. The kidneys are the major site of deposition; renal damage includes reversible proteinuria, acute tubular necrosis and nephrotic syndrome. Gastrointestinal effects include a metallic taste, gingivostomatitis, nausea and hypersalivation. A single case report (Tang 2006, PMID 16912361) documented a woman with nephrotic syndrome whose proteinuria remitted 9 months after stopping the cream.
